title: Excel formulas — reference for this workbook
intro_md:
The Excel tab is a small spreadsheet grid powered by **HyperFormula** (an open-source Excel-compatible formula engine). It is not Microsoft Excel: it evaluates ~400 Excel functions faithfully, but there are **no pivot tables, charts, macros, formatting or dynamic-array spill ranges**. Only functions listed on this page are taught and graded.

**Workbook**: sheets `Students` (120 rows), `Enrollments` (300), `Sections` (236), `Courses` (136), `Departments` (24), `Employees` (100 faculty), `Terms` (6) and `Answers`. Headers are in row 1; data starts in row 2. Dates are real dates.

**Using the grid**: click a cell and type (or use the formula bar), **Enter** to commit, **Esc** to cancel, arrows / Tab to move, Shift+click to select a range, **Ctrl+D** or the *Fill down* button to copy the top formula down a selection (relative references adjust). While typing a formula, clicking another cell inserts its reference. Cross-sheet references: `Students!F2:F121`. Lock a reference with `$`: `Sections!$A$2:$E$237`.

**Not available** (will show `#NAME?`): `CONCAT` (use `CONCATENATE` or `&`), `AVERAGEIFS` (use `SUMIFS/COUNTIFS` or `AVERAGEIF`), `LET`, `LAMBDA`, `RANK`, `SORTBY`, `TEXTSPLIT`, and dynamic-array spilling. `XLOOKUP`, `FILTER`, `UNIQUE` exist in the engine but are deliberately out of scope for v1.
sandbox_md: Sandbox workbook: every sheet is editable, nothing is graded. Put a formula in **Answers!B2** (selected for you) or anywhere else.

sections.heading: Logical
sections.body_md: `IF(test, yes, no)`, `IFS(test1, v1, test2, v2, …, TRUE, default)`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `IFERROR(value, fallback)`, `IFNA`, `ISBLANK`, `ISNUMBER`, `ISTEXT`, `ISERROR`. `TRUE`/`FALSE` literals work. Comparison operators: `=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`.

sections.heading: Conditional aggregates
sections.body_md: `COUNTIF(range, criteria)`, `COUNTIFS(r1, c1, r2, c2, …)`, `SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range)`, `SUMIFS(sum_range, r1, c1, …)`, `AVERAGEIF(range, criteria, avg_range)`, `MAXIFS(max_range, r1, c1)`, `MINIFS`. Criteria are text: `"MO"`, `">=3.5"`, `"<>completed"`, or a cell reference. Wildcards `*` and `?` work in text criteria.

sections.heading: Lookups: VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH
sections.body_md: `VLOOKUP(value, table, col_index, FALSE)` — exact match, the key must be the first column of `table`. `HLOOKUP` is the horizontal twin. `MATCH(value, one_row_or_column, 0)` returns the position; `INDEX(range, row, [col])` reads from it — together they look up to the left and do **two-way** lookups: `INDEX(table, MATCH(row_key, key_col, 0), MATCH(col_name, header_row, 0))`. Lock table ranges with `$` before filling down.

sections.heading: Text
sections.body_md: `LEFT(t, n)`, `RIGHT(t, n)`, `MID(t, start, n)`, `LEN`, `UPPER`, `LOWER`, `PROPER`, `TRIM` (collapses spaces), `CLEAN`, `CONCATENATE(a, b, …)` or `a & b`, `TEXTJOIN(sep, ignore_empty, range)`, `SUBSTITUTE(t, old, new)`, `REPLACE`, `FIND` (case-sensitive) / `SEARCH`, `EXACT`, `VALUE(text)` → number, `TEXT(number, format)` → text, `REPT`, `CHAR`, `CODE`. No `CONCAT`.

sections.heading: Dates
sections.body_md: Dates are serial numbers displayed as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `DATE(y, m, d)`, `TODAY()`, `YEAR`, `MONTH`, `DAY`, `WEEKDAY`, `EDATE(d, months)`, `EOMONTH(d, 0)`, `DAYS(end, start)`, `DATEDIF(start, end, "Y"|"M"|"D")` (complete years/months/days), `NETWORKDAYS`, `DATEVALUE("2024-01-16")`, `TEXT(d, "yyyy-mm")`. Subtracting two dates gives days.

examples.label: Days until the end of the month

sections.heading: Array-style formulas: SUMPRODUCT and IF over ranges
sections.body_md: Array arithmetic is enabled in this workbook, so a comparison over a range (`Students!D2:D121="MO"`) yields an array of TRUE/FALSE that behaves like 1/0 in arithmetic. `SUMPRODUCT((cond1)*(cond2)*values)` sums with multiple criteria; `SUMPRODUCT(--(cond))` counts. `LARGE(IF(cond, values), n)`, `MAX(IF(...))`, `AVERAGE(IF(...))` filter before aggregating — no Ctrl+Shift+Enter needed here. Results are single values; spilling arrays into neighbouring cells is not supported.
